outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no proof, disproof or unconditional advance on the four exponentials conjecture has been found. The in-window items are two conditional reductions to the conjecture (Dasgupta and Kakde 2024; Prasad 2025), one reformulation via Schanuel's conjecture and multiplicative Zilber-Pink (Pila 2025), generic or neighbouring Schanuel-type and exponential-independence results that do not cover its specific tuples, and one unverified 2025 forum claim about a Schanuel question that I could not trace to its source.
problem_asks: (a) For any two complex numbers x1, x2 that are linearly independent over Q, and any two complex numbers y1, y2 that are linearly independent over Q: (b) at least one of the four numbers e^(x1*y1), e^(x1*y2), e^(x2*y1), e^(x2*y2) is transcendental. The bullet says 'combinations of irrationals'; I read this as the products x_i*y_j of such numbers, and the standard statement (Wikipedia; Waldschmidt's notes; Schneider 1957) is over the complex numbers, so the real case is a special case rather than the whole claim. Equivalent form carrying the same demand (not a separate part): if each exp(lambda_ij) is algebraic and the rows and the columns of the 2x2 matrix (lambda_ij) are each Q-linearly independent, then the matrix has rank 2. Not in the bullet's words but a named companion open case in the literature: the p-adic version (Waldschmidt's 2022 survey, read via search excerpt). Parts to account for: the hypotheses (two Q-independent pairs, complex) and the conclusion (one of four exponentials transcendental).

events.what_happened: Damien Roy and Michel Waldschmidt, 'Quadratic relations between logarithms of algebraic numbers', Proc. Japan Acad. Ser. A 71 (1995). Proves the four exponentials statement when the field Q(x1, x2, y1, y2) has transcendence degree 1 over Q, using Wirsing's theorem and Laurent-type interpolation determinants, and announces that the 2x2 determinant can be replaced by any homogeneous quadratic polynomial. The title, journal and theorem statement come from search excerpts and from Waldschmidt's lecture notes; the Project Euclid page returned a bot-check and was not read.
events.delivers: Proves the conjecture for quadruples where Q(x1, x2, y1, y2) has transcendence degree 1 over Q (the four logarithms span a one-dimensional transcendence field). The restriction is to that case; the excerpts show no wider class.
events.remains: Every quadruple where the transcendence degree of Q(x1, x2, y1, y2) over Q is 2, 3 or 4; the strong form; the p-adic form.

checked_by.qualification: Transcendence theorist; co-author of the 1995 paper, so not an independent reading
checked_by.what_they_did: Describes the degree-one case as the only solved special case of the conjecture in his lecture notes (search excerpts of 2003 and later notes)

events.direction: Toward the conjecture: proves a restricted case (transcendence degree 1).

events.what_happened: G. (Guy) Diaz, Journal de Theorie des Nombres de Bordeaux 19 (2007), article on products and quotients of linear combinations of logarithms of algebraic numbers. Its English abstract, read via search excerpt, says that Roy's strong six exponentials theorem combined with complex conjugation gives partial results for the strong four exponentials conjecture. The emis PDF returned a 503 error and was not read; the excerpt gives a received date of October 2005.
events.revisions: Received October 2005 per excerpt; the first public written version may be earlier. Not checked.
events.delivers: Partial results toward the strong four exponentials conjecture (entries in the algebraic-coefficient span of 1 and logarithms), via the strong six exponentials theorem and complex conjugation. Which cases, and whether any gives the plain statement for complex x and y, is not visible in the excerpt.
events.remains: The plain four exponentials conjecture as stated, and the strong form outside whatever cases the paper covers.

checked_by.who: Journal de Theorie des Nombres de Bordeaux (refereed)

events.direction: Toward the strong form, in restricted cases; does not settle the plain statement.

events.what_happened: Laurent Habsieger, 'A few remarks related to the four exponentials conjecture', Publicationes Mathematicae Debrecen 70 (2007), 179-194 (DOI 10.5486/PMD.2007.3505). Specialises the conjecture to powers of 2 and 3: asks whether a real t with 2^t and 3^t both integers must itself be an integer, and (per search excerpts) proves the three-base variant in which 2^t, 3^t and 5^t are all integers. The publisher page was opened for metadata only; the abstract and body were not readable.
events.delivers: A specialisation. It states the two-base case (2^t and 3^t integers force t integer), which is a special case of the four exponentials statement, and (per excerpt) proves the three-base variant. The three-base variant has an extra hypothesis (5^t integer), so it is a weaker statement than the two-base case and does not settle it.
events.remains: The two-base case (a special case of the conjecture) and the general conjecture.
events.direction: Specialisation; leaves the two-base case open. Neither way on the general conjecture.

events.what_happened: Jonathan Pila, 'Entire functions sharing arguments of integrality, II', Publicationes Mathematicae Debrecen 73 (2008), 215-231 (DOI 10.5486/PMD.2008.4212). The publisher page was opened for metadata only; the abstract was not visible. Per a search excerpt, the paper gives a slight strengthening of a special case of the six exponentials theorem, and states that the special case of the four exponentials conjecture with all four numbers positive reals and all four exponentials integers is still open.
events.delivers: A strengthening of a special case of the six exponentials theorem, not of the four exponentials conjecture. It explicitly leaves open the four-exponential case with positive real x and y and integer-valued exponentials.
events.remains: The positive-real, integer-exponential special case, and the general conjecture.
events.direction: Neither way; records a special case as open.

events.what_happened: Garth Warner, 'The Exponential World', arXiv:2105.05809 (v1, 11 May 2021, math.HO), an introduction to transcendental number theory. The fetched arXiv abstract page does not mention the conjecture. A search excerpt of the PDF says the text proves that the set of real t with 2^t, 3^t and 5^t all integers is the natural numbers, and presents the two-base question as open. The 'long-standing open problem' wording also came from a search excerpt, not from the fetched page.
events.delivers: Per excerpt: the three-base result (2, 3 and 5), which is weaker than the two-base specialisation for the reason given for Habsieger 2007. The two-base question is posed as open.
events.remains: The two-base case and the general conjecture.
events.direction: Neighbouring specialisation; weaker three-base statement; neither way on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Mao-Sheng Li, 'Four exponentials conjecture of Drinfeld modules', Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 149 (2021), 2375-2380. Proves the function-field analogue for Drinfeld modules, building on Chang and Papanikolas's algebraic independence of Drinfeld logarithms at algebraic points. The AMS page returned 403; the title, journal and page numbers come from search results.
events.delivers: The four exponentials statement for Drinfeld modules (positive characteristic). This is an analogue in a different setting, not the classical complex or p-adic statement.
events.remains: The classical complex four exponentials conjecture as stated, and the p-adic version.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society (refereed)

events.direction: Analogue in a different field; does not bear on the classical statement's truth.

events.what_happened: Samit Dasgupta and Mahesh Kakde, 'Ranks of matrices of logarithms of algebraic numbers II: the matrix coefficient conjecture', arXiv:2408.08178 (submitted 15 August 2024; single version). States the Matrix Coefficient Conjecture: if a square matrix of logarithms of algebraic numbers is singular, then after a rational change of basis on each side it can be made to have a vanishing coefficient. The introduction, read through the arXiv HTML fetch (quoted via a summarising tool, so the wording is close but not verbatim), says that the conjecture is equivalent to the four exponentials conjecture only for 2x2 matrices (n = 2), and that it also implies Leopoldt-type and Gross-Kuz'min statements. The paper calls these open problems and proves only the conditional implications. The Duke publications listing (search excerpt, not opened) gives Advances in Mathematics as the venue; the arXiv record gives no journal reference.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (15 Aug 2024). Journal venue per Duke listing excerpt; not verified.
events.delivers: A reformulation. A new conjecture (the Matrix Coefficient Conjecture) is stated and, per the introduction, is equivalent to the four exponentials statement for 2x2 matrices. No unconditional instance of the statement is proved.
events.remains: All of the four exponentials statement, since the equivalence moves it onto the new conjecture rather than proving it.
events.direction: Neither way on the conjecture; reduces it to a new conjecture.

events.what_happened: Heinrich Massold, 'Transcendence degrees of fields generated by exponentials of products', arXiv:2506.01123 (v1, 1 June 2025, math.NT). Studies the transcendence degree T of Q(exp(theta_i * kappa_j)) for Q-linearly independent tuples theta (length m) and kappa (length n). Per the abstract (opened): the conjectured estimate T >= mn/(m+n) - 1 is not proved in general; a weaker lower estimate is proved; the stronger estimate is reduced to a conjecture on intersections of subvarieties of split tori. The abstract does not mention the four exponentials conjecture.
events.delivers: A weaker lower bound on the transcendence degree of the field generated by mn exponentials of products, for general m and n; the stronger bound is reduced to a subvariety conjecture. For m = n = 2 (the four exponentials configuration) the conjectured bound as quoted gives 0, so it carries no content for the conjecture. A transcendence degree of at least 1 at m = n = 2 would give the conjecture's conclusion, and whether the weaker bound reaches that was not checked in the body.
events.remains: The four exponentials statement is not addressed in the abstract; the general estimate remains open.
events.direction: Neither way on the conjecture; neighbouring bound with unestablished relevance to the m = n = 2 case.

events.what_happened: Michel Waldschmidt, 'Schanuel property for elliptic and quasi-elliptic functions', arXiv:2504.14041 (submitted 18 April 2025; one version). Per the abstract (opened): a strong Schanuel-type property holds for almost all tuples of complex numbers, and the paper gives examples of algebraically independent elliptic, exponential and related functions. The abstract does not mention the four exponentials conjecture. A search excerpt reports publication in the Hardy-Ramanujan Journal (volume 48, 2025; publication date reported as 27 April 2026); that page was not opened.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv. Journal version reported with a 2026 publication date (search excerpt).
events.delivers: A generic result: a strong Schanuel-type property for almost all tuples. Schanuel's conjecture implies the four exponentials statement, but a statement for almost all tuples does not cover the specific tuples the four exponentials statement concerns, so it settles no specified instance.
events.remains: The four exponentials statement for all quadruples; the generic result says nothing about a specified quadruple.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (reported volume 48, 2025; publication date 27 April 2026, per search excerpt)

events.direction: Neither way on the conjecture; a generic Schanuel-type result.

events.what_happened: Veekesh Kumar and Riccardo Tosi, 'A simultaneous approximation problem for exponentials and logarithms', arXiv:2505.20957 (submitted 27 May 2025, math.NT). Per the abstract page (opened; the abstract itself was longer than the fetch could quote): for two non-zero algebraic numbers with irrational log ratio and a quadratic irrational beta, two coprime integer-coefficient polynomials do not take too-small values at a point built from these quantities, and a measure of algebraic independence is established for related numbers. Neither the four exponentials conjecture nor Schanuel's conjecture appears on the abstract page.
events.delivers: A measure of algebraic independence and an approximation estimate for numbers built from logarithms and exponentials of algebraic numbers. It is not an instance of the four exponentials statement and does not address a quadruple of exponentials.
events.direction: Neighbouring; does not bear on the conjectured conclusion.

events.what_happened: Dipendra Prasad, 'Some questions in Diophantine approximation: real and p-adics', arXiv:2505.15744 (submitted 21 May 2025; one version; math.NT). Section 4 is headed 'Four exponential conjecture'. The arXiv HTML was read via a summarising fetch, so the wording is close but not verbatim. The paper says that its Conjecture 1, specialised from R_{K/Q}(G_m) to G_m x G_m, 'is equivalent to the four exponential conjecture'. It calls the four exponential conjecture a conjecture (not proved), calls the six exponential theorem a theorem, and notes that it is not known whether the determinant of the log matrix for 2, 3, p, q is nonzero. The paper claims no proof of the four exponentials statement. The arXiv abstract does not mention it.
events.delivers: A reduction. A conjecture of the paper, in the G_m x G_m case, is equivalent to the four exponentials statement. No unconditional result. The paper does not say its Conjecture 1 in the R_{K/Q}(G_m) form is equivalent to it.
events.remains: The whole four exponentials statement, and the paper's conjecture in the R_{K/Q}(G_m) form.
events.direction: Neither way on the conjecture; reduces it to the paper's G_m x G_m conjecture.

events.what_happened: Jonathan Pila, 'Combining the conjectures of Schanuel and Zilber-Pink', Rendiconti Lincei - Matematica e Applicazioni 36 (2025), 653-670 (DOI 10.4171/RLM/1086). Per the EMS abstract page (opened): 'We formulate a conjecture that is strictly equivalent to the conjunction of Schanuel's conjecture and the multiplicative Zilber-Pink conjecture.' The page gives submission on 27 April 2025 and acceptance on 1 July 2025; an Oxford ORA record gives publication on 4 March 2026. I found no arXiv posting, so the first public written version is not pinned down. The abstract does not mention the four exponentials conjecture.
events.revisions: Submitted 27 Apr 2025; accepted 1 Jul 2025; publication reported as 2025 volume and 4 Mar 2026 (ORA). No arXiv version found, so the date is the year of the journal volume, not a first-posting date.
events.delivers: A reformulation. It states one conjecture equivalent to the conjunction of Schanuel's conjecture and multiplicative Zilber-Pink, and proves neither. Schanuel's conjecture implies the four exponentials statement, so the equivalence gives no unconditional instance.

checked_by.who: Rendiconti Lincei - Matematica e Applicazioni (Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei / EMS Press)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the article for publication (1 July 2025 per the EMS page)

events.direction: Neither way on the conjecture; a reformulation.

The quoted wording suggests a particular question rather than the whole conjecture, and nothing I could read shows what was proved.

events.what_happened: Cristiana Bertolin, 'Algebraic independence of the exponential and Weierstrass p-functions', arXiv:2609.15294 (submitted 14 September 2026; v1). Per the abstract page (opened; the abstract was partly paraphrased by the fetch tool): for a lattice with complex multiplication, exponentials of Q-linearly independent algebraic numbers together with p-values at k-linearly independent algebraic points are algebraically independent over the algebraic closure of Q; the result generalises Lindemann-Weierstrass and Philippon-Wustholz. The page does not mention the four exponentials conjecture or Schanuel's conjecture.
events.delivers: Algebraic independence of exponentials of algebraic numbers and Weierstrass p-values on CM lattices. It is a Lindemann-Weierstrass-type result for a different function, and does not involve products x_i*y_j of pairs, so it has no direct bearing on the conjecture.
events.direction: Neither way on the conjecture; neighbouring result.

summary: Nothing settles the four exponentials conjecture in the window, and the conjecture is still listed as unproven. The Wikipedia article (read through a summarising fetch, so quotes are paraphrase; last edited 16 September 2025) calls the conjecture unproven, and calls the three exponentials conjecture still open. In the window I found six items bearing on it. Two are conditional reductions: Dasgupta and Kakde (arXiv 2408.08178, August 2024) state a Matrix Coefficient Conjecture that they say is equivalent to the statement for 2x2 matrices, and Prasad (arXiv 2505.15744, May 2025) says his G_m x G_m conjecture is equivalent to it. Pila (Rend. Lincei 2025) gives a conjecture equivalent to Schanuel plus multiplicative Zilber-Pink. Waldschmidt (2025), Massold (2025), Kumar and Tosi (2025) and Bertolin (2026) are generic or neighbouring results that do not address a specified quadruple. The sixth is an unverified 2025 forum reply, quoted in the benchmark paper arXiv 2508.17580, claiming an answer to a Schanuel question. Schanuel's conjecture implies the four exponentials statement, so a proof of Schanuel would settle it; but the quoted wording suggests a narrower question, and I could not reach its source, so I record it as unresolved rather than as movement. Before the window, the only proven restricted case I found is the transcendence-degree-one case (Roy and Waldschmidt, 1995). Other items are analogues (Li 2021, Drinfeld modules), specialisations (Habsieger 2007, Warner 2021, Pila 2008) and partial results toward the strong form (Diaz 2007). The bullet's wording, 'combinations of irrationals', is loose; I read it as the complex statement, which is the standard form. No source names an AI system in connection with this conjecture; the AI-tagged results I met (Erdos-problem solutions, a reported Jacobian counterexample, a ChatGPT/Claude declaration in arXiv 2609.05047 on Gatheral's conjecture) concern other problems and I did not research them further. I also noted, without verifying, the Wikipedia claim that the weak statement follows from Bertrand's conjecture. Several primary papers could not be read: the Roy-Waldschmidt paper (Project Euclid bot-check page), the Li paper (AMS 403), Diaz (emis 503), and Waldschmidt's 2004 and 2022 surveys (binary PDFs). Their statements come from search excerpts and are marked as such.
competing_reading: Read Dasgupta-Kakde and Prasad as the problem's first new content since 2024: each turns the conjecture into an equivalent statement about a specific object (a matrix of logarithms, a G_m x G_m conjecture), and someone who counts equivalences as progress could give them weight. Against that, neither proves anything, and equivalence with an open conjecture moves the problem's status by nothing. A second reading takes the 2025 Schanuel reply seriously: if its answer proved Schanuel's conjecture it would settle the four exponentials statement by implication, which would make it the decisive event; the missing source and the narrower wording keep that reading unsupported. A third reading treats the 1995 degree-one case as partial settlement before the window, which changes how to read the window's silence: the problem is not wholly open, only the general case is.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The forum thread quoted in arXiv 2508.17580 (Appendix E.4.3, or the Math Overflow post it cites), with its date, author, and what was proved. (2) The 1995 Roy-Waldschmidt paper, to confirm the degree-one theorem and its hypotheses. (3) The text of Waldschmidt's 2022 Festschrift survey, to confirm the open-status sentence and the list of special cases as of 2022. (4) Dasgupta and Kakde's journal version and any paper citing it, to see whether the equivalence was accepted or used. (5) Prasad's Conjecture 1 in the R_{K/Q}(G_m) form, to see whether it also implies the four exponentials statement. (6) A zbMATH or MathSciNet citation search for the conjecture, which returned 403 here.

dead_ends: No AI system is named in any source about the four exponentials conjecture. AI-tagged results found in search concerned other problems: Erdos-problem solutions with GPT-5.2 Pro and others; AlphaProof Nexus and Aletheia; a May 2026 OpenAI unit-distance disproof; a reported July 2026 Jacobian counterexample via Claude (aggregator source, unverified); a reported GPT-5.6 cycle-double-cover claim (aggregator source). None is on this conjecture, and I did not research them further.
Gatheral's Conjecture Revisited (arXiv 2609.05047) has a generative-AI declaration naming ChatGPT and Claude, but it is about a finance conjecture; not relevant.

Dasgupta I (arXiv 2303.02037, March 2023) is expository and proposes the Matrix Coefficient Conjecture as a necessary condition for singular matrices; it contains no four exponentials result, so it is not an event.
Universal completeness of exponentials (arXiv 2609.20805, Sep 2026) concerns Fourier-type completeness in L^p; no mention of the conjecture or Schanuel, so not an event.

Bleybel (arXiv 1310.3777, withdrawn) and Marques (arXiv 0812.4178, withdrawn) are Schanuel-related withdrawn claims from before the window; neither concerns the four exponentials statement, so neither is an event. Seen in search only.

Bays, Kirby and Wilkie (arXiv 0810.4457, 2008): Schanuel-type result for almost all real exponents; before the window and about Schanuel rather than the four exponentials statement. Seen in search only.
Zilber-Pink equivalence to the four exponentials statement: searched for; no source found. The equivalence claimed in search results was for the Schanuel and Zilber-Pink conjunction, not for FEC.
Schneider's eight problems: searched for progress since 2024; none found. The eighth problem was solved by Waldschmidt in 1973 (search excerpt); the first is this conjecture.
